# Sales Trend Overview

A **line chart** is the best choice to show this dataset because it makes the month-to-month movement easy to see at a glance. A bar chart can work too, but the line chart is stronger for highlighting the overall trend.

# Month-over-Month Sales Changes

Formula: **MoM change = Current month sales − Previous month sales**

| Month | Sales | MoM Change | MoM % |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Jan | 120 | — | — |
| Feb | 135 | +15 | +12.5% |
| Mar | 128 | -7 | -5.2% |
| Apr | 150 | +22 | +17.2% |
| May | 162 | +12 | +8.0% |
| Jun | 158 | -4 | -2.5% |

# Manager Takeaways

- **Overall trend is upward.** Sales rose from **120 in Jan** to **158 in Jun**, a net gain of **38** units, so the business is growing over the half-year.
- **Growth is uneven, with dips in Mar and Jun.** That suggests the manager should review what changed in those months, then double down on whatever likely drove the stronger jumps in **Apr and May**.

# Quick Actions

- Action: [Button: View line chart setup](https://www.datawrapper.de/charts/line-chart/)
- Action: [Button: Learn chart choices](https://www.tableau.com/learn/articles/charts-graphs)

# Sources

- Chart guidance: https://www.tableau.com/learn/articles/charts-graphs
- Line chart basics: https://www.datawrapper.de/charts/line-chart/
